OQ-02.decision: Playwright (Java binding com.microsoft.playwright:playwright) running locally on the backend pod — NOT Selenium Grid, NOT cloud Playwright
implications: Playwright browser binaries (chromium/firefox/webkit) bundled into the backend container image — adds ~200-400MB per browser.

Proposed package: backend/src/main/java/com/citi/put/checks/studio/playwright/ as the Playwright adapter.

OQ-03.question: Retention policy for tags and secrets tables
OQ-03.decision: Proposal by @architect, based on domain semantics

tags.rationale: Tags are low-cardinality metadata (~100s-1000s rows across the platform). Orphaned tags (no referencing check/csi) are not a correctness issue; junction tables (check_tags, csi_tags) auto-clean via ON DELETE CASCADE when a check or CSI is hard-deleted. Cost of retention is negligible. Risk of accidental deletion > benefit of cleanup.

secrets.retention: INDEFINITE for active references; respect expires_at at resolution time
secrets.rationale: The `secrets` table stores only vault REFERENCES (reference_id, label, last_four), never the secret value. A reference with expires_at in the past is still useful audit data (shows which check once used which vault entry). Hard-deleting breaks check history traceability.
secrets.action: On execution attempt with a secret whose expires_at < NOW(), FAIL the check execution with error='Secret reference expired' and emit audit event. Do not delete the row. Dashboard surfaces 'stale secret' counts via a metric.

debt_items.change: Add rows for Tags (indefinite) and Secret References (indefinite; expiry enforced at use-time)

OQ-04.question: Schedule endpoint shape: inline with checks, or dedicated /schedules?
implications: New endpoints required (ARCH §12 does not list these — amend as DEBT-03):
GET    /api/v1/schedules                 — list all (filter by check_id, enabled)
POST   /api/v1/schedules                 — create (body includes check_id)
GET    /api/v1/schedules/{id}            — fetch one
PUT    /api/v1/schedules/{id}            — replace
PATCH  /api/v1/schedules/{id}/enabled    — toggle enabled (lightweight no-op-friendly)
DELETE /api/v1/schedules/{id}            — delete (cascades from check delete too)
One schedule per check enforced by `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_schedules_check` (ARCH §7.1).
GET /api/v1/checks/{id} response embeds the schedule in a nested field for client convenience (read-only, mirrors /schedules/{id}).

OQ-05.question: Partition maintenance strategy for execution_results without DB-team dependency
OQ-05.decision: App-managed partitions via Spring @Scheduled + Flyway for base table only
OQ-05.decided_by: user (constraint: no DB team dependency, easiest to maintain)

rejected_alternatives.reason_rejected: Requires CREATE EXTENSION privilege and pg_partman installation on the managed RDS cluster — blocked by DB team dependency constraint.
Violates user constraint 'prefer not depend on external teams'.

design.base_table_in_flyway: V1__init.sql creates the parent execution_results table declared PARTITION BY RANGE (started_at) PLUS the current month's partition. No future partitions in Flyway.
design.runtime_partition_creator: A Spring bean ExecutionResultsPartitionScheduler annotated @Scheduled(cron='0 0 3 25 * ?') (03:00 UTC on the 25th of each month) runs raw DDL: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS execution_results_{yyyy}_{mm} PARTITION OF execution_results FOR VALUES FROM ('{yyyy}-{mm}-01') TO ('{next_yyyy}-{next_mm}-01'); Safe to re-run (IF NOT EXISTS).
design.bootstrapping_safety: Application also runs the same DDL on startup for (current_month, current_month+1, current_month+2) to cover freshly-deployed environments. Idempotent.
design.pruning: Old partitions (older than 1 year per NFR-RET-01) detached by the same scheduler once a month: ALTER TABLE execution_results DETACH PARTITION execution_results_{old}; DROP TABLE execution_results_{old};
design.failure_mode: If the scheduler fails to create next month's partition, INSERTs starting the 1st of next month will raise 'no partition of relation found'. Mitigation: health check exposes a /actuator/health/partitions indicator that fails if the next-month partition is missing by the 28th — alerts surface BEFORE user impact.

why_easiest_to_maintain: Zero external dependencies (no extension, no DBA ticket).
One Spring bean + one Flyway migration. Lives in backend/src/main/java/com/citi/put/checks/scheduling/partitioning/.
Testable via Testcontainers-PostgreSQL (CI) and Zonky embedded (local) with identical semantics.
Same pattern reused for ui_test_executions (monthly) and report_executions (quarterly) — all three auto-maintained.

scope.justification: Greenfield backend — 37 FRs spanning 7 bounded contexts (csi, checks, scheduling, studio, reports, users, secrets). ~20 entities, Flyway migrations, DTO/entity/service/controller layers, 7 CheckExecutor implementations, partitioned tables + materialized view + DB triggers. Conservatively 150-250 Java source files at M6 completion.
evidence: ARCH §7 Database Schema (13 tables + 1 materialized view + 2 triggers)

integration.justification: Nine external system integrations, each with its own protocol, auth, failure mode, and data contract. This is the single largest complexity driver.
evidence: Playwright (local, in-container) — OQ-02 resolution (not counted as external)

infrastructure.justification: Kubernetes deployment with multiple replicas, managed PostgreSQL RDS, managed Redis (M6), S3 bucket provisioning, Vault policy/AppRole setup, Playwright-bundled container image (~1-2GB vs. a typical JRE image ~200MB). Score tempered to 4 (not 5) because the architecture deliberately minimizes infra team dependency: Zonky embedded for local dev (ARCH §5), app-managed partitions (OQ-05), Caffeine-first caching (M1-M5 before Redis at M6).
evidence: OQ-02 implications: dedicated 'studio-runner' StatefulSet for concurrency
OQ-05 resolution: self-maintained partitions reduce infra dependency

knowledge.justification: Core stack (Java 21, Spring Boot 3, JPA, Gradle KTS, JUnit 5) is well-known to a typical senior Java team. Less-common knowledge required: virtual-thread task executors under load, Zonky embedded PostgreSQL integration patterns, declarative partitioning with app-side maintenance, MapStruct for polymorphic JSONB types, Playwright Java binding (less documented than the Node version), Vault AppRole auth flow. Score 3 = standard team with a handful of knowledge gaps research must close.
evidence: OQ-02 — Playwright Java is the less-documented binding
OQ-05 — app-managed partitioning is uncommon in Spring Boot apps

risk.justification: Regulated financial services (Citibank), 99.95% uptime SLO (NFR-AVAIL-01), security-critical (SSO + RBAC + Vault), handles credentials for 4 external monitoring systems, executes UI tests against production URLs (risk of triggering real events on misconfigured tests), report emails go to IT Directors (reputational risk on false positives/negatives).
evidence: PRD §4 Personas: Robert (IT Director) consumes reports
FR-STUDIO-02: UI tests can execute against live citi.com per PRD §6 example

rationale: Score 22/25 places this comfortably in COMPLEX. Scope, integration, and risk each max at 5 — any of those three alone would push this out of SIMPLE. Infrastructure at 4 reflects the deliberate design choice to minimize external-team dependency (Zonky, app-managed partitions, Caffeine-first caching) — these mitigations shave one point off what would otherwise also be 5. Knowledge at 3 is the single non-critical dimension.
